( temp article)

The [[architecture of Vurahi]] over the centuries has greatly developed from [[Kingdom of Areoix Lie|The kingdom of Areoix Lie]] architecture to [[Arten modern and contemporary architecture]]. Vurahi was once one of the world's main epicentres of Classical architecture, developing new forms such as the dome and the vault. [[The Imperial style of Architecture|The Imperial style]] in the 11th, 12th and 13th centuries was also widely used in [[Architecture of Vurahi|Vury architecture]], and later the city became one of the main centres of Renaissance and Baroque architecture. Vurahis cityscape is also widely Neoclassical and Imperial in style.

The city also encloses the 36 hectare [[Imperial Gardens of Vurahi|The Imperial Gardens]] that contains protected natural forest and fynbos along with a variety of animals and birds. There are over 7,000 species in cultivation at [[Imperial Gardens of Vurahi|The Imperial Gardens]], including many rare and threatened species of the [[Virauzau Floristic Region]]. In 1742 this Region, including [[Imperial Gardens of Vurahi|The Imperial Gardens]], was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
